paper_metadata.title: High-throughput investigation of elemental substitution effects on precipitation of TCP phases in Ni-based superalloys containing Re and Ru

evidence.quote: to explore the precipitation of topologically close packed (TCP) phases in Ni-based superalloys following heat treatment at 1100 ◦C for 1000 h
The middle alloy represents a Ni-based superalloy with a composition of 0Co-5Ru-1Mo-6.5Re-6Al-3.5Cr-6Ta-5W-Bal.Ni (wt%), named as the base alloy.
The left alloy named as alloy 16Co3Ru was made from the composition of the base alloy by increasing Co content to 16.0 wt% and reducing Ru content to 3.0 wt%.
the right alloy named as alloy 8Co4Mo3Re was also formed from the composition of the base alloy by adjusting Co, Mo, and Re contents to 8.0 wt%, 4.0 wt%, and 3.0 wt%, respectively.

mechanisms.name: reduction of gamma-phase supersaturation and lattice mismatch with P phase

evidence.quote: Analyses showed that reducing the supersaturation of the γ phase and its lattice mismatch with the P phase, thereby decreasing the precipitation driving force while increasing resistance, accounts for the suppression of P phase precipitation by such elemental substitutions.
